chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanee, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever divorces [his wife] without witnesses, it is not valid."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid divorce in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam underscores the procedural integrity of divorce in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the absence of witnesses renders the talaq legally void (laysa bi-shay'). It reflects the scholarly consensus on the necessity of public verification to prevent disputes, aligning with the Quranic injunction to record divorces with witnesses as a safeguard for both parties.
